title: Rollout controller: block canary promotion on Optimize quality-gate failure
creator: Paula Mendes
description:
Context
Optimize can propose cost-saving config diffs (batching, caching, quantization profiles) that can change outputs. Quality gates are required before applying a recommendation. This ticket wires those gate results into the rollout controller so that we cannot accidentally promote canaries (or complete rollouts) when gates failed / are missing.

Scope
- Enforce gate status at rollout-controller promotion boundaries (canary -> 10%/25% -> 50% -> 100%, depending on policy).
- Define halt/rollback behavior when a gate fails or becomes invalid mid-rollout.
- Notifications: who gets notified, where, and with what context (gate run link + failure reasons).
- Defense-in-depth: even if Optimize UI/API is bypassed, rollout controller must still prevent unsafe promotion.

Non-goals
- Designing new rollout UI components in Console (tracked in ENG-3925 / DES-611).
- Full Private/on-prem automation (initially manual workflow per PRD).

Proposed policy (MVP)
Gate enforcement applies to rollouts that include Optimize-owned config diffs of type: batching policy, prefix/KV cache settings, quant profile.

Promotion checks
At each promotion event, rollout controller must evaluate:
1) Gate required?
- Determine based on: config-diff contains gated knobs AND route/account tier policy (see per-route policy work).
- If unknown: default to “required” for gated knobs in hosted API.

2) Gate state allowed?
- ALLOW promotion only if gate_state in {PASSED, OVERRIDDEN}.
- BLOCK promotion if gate_state in {PENDING, RUNNING, FAILED, CANCELED, TIMEOUT, UNKNOWN, NOT_FOUND}.

3) Gate freshness / applicability
- Gate result must match (config_diff_hash, baseline_ref, model_version, hardware_sku where applicable).
- Gate result must be within TTL (default 7 days) OR explicitly pinned to this rollout (preferred).
- If config diff changes (even semantically equivalent) after gate run started: treat as NOT_FOUND and block.

4) Override handling
- OVERRIDDEN allowed only if:
  - override not expired
  - override reason provided
  - override recorded with approver + scope (route, diff hash)
- If override expires mid-rollout, further promotions block (existing traffic stays at current canary percentage). Operator can: (a) extend override, (b) run gates again, (c) roll back.

Halt and rollback behavior
- If a promotion attempt is blocked due to missing/failed gate:
  - Do not change traffic weights.
  - Mark rollout step as “HALTED_QUALITY_GATE” with reason codes.
  - Emit audit event and notify.

- If gate fails while canary is already running (i.e., gate execution overlaps with early canary):
  - Immediately halt further promotion.
  - For canary weights > 0: trigger automatic rollback to previous stable config if policy says “auto_rollback_on_gate_fail=true”.
  - Default for hosted API MVP: auto rollback ON for self-serve tiers; OFF for enterprise (halt + require human decision) to avoid surprising changes, but strongly recommend rollback in the UI.

- If rollback fails (e.g., config apply fails):
  - Escalate to oncall (SRE + platform) and keep rollout halted.

State machine integration points
- Rollout controller currently uses states: CREATED -> CANARY_RUNNING -> PROMOTING -> COMPLETED / HALTED / ROLLED_BACK.
- Add new terminal-ish halt reason: HALTED_QUALITY_GATE.
- Add structured reason codes:
  - QUALITY_GATE_NOT_FOUND
  - QUALITY_GATE_PENDING
  - QUALITY_GATE_FAILED
  - QUALITY_GATE_TIMEOUT
  - QUALITY_GATE_MISMATCH (diff hash / baseline / model version mismatch)
  - QUALITY_GATE_OVERRIDE_EXPIRED

API / data requirements
- Rollout controller must be able to query Optimize service for gate summary by (route_id, rollout_id, config_diff_hash).
- Minimum response needed:
  - gate_run_id
  - gate_state
  - started_at / completed_at
  - gate_tier (smoke/full)
  - failure_reasons (top-level)
  - override: status, expires_at, approver
  - artifacts_url (for Console deep link)

- For MVP, polling is acceptable at promotion time (no continuous stream). Cache for 30s to avoid thundering herd during batch promotions.

Notifications
- Slack: post to #eng-sre for auto-rollbacks; post to #eng-ml for repeated failures by prompt set; post to #product for blocked customer-facing rollouts > 2h.
- Pager: only when rollback is attempted and fails OR gate-related block rate spikes (handled via alerting ticket).
- Include in payload:
  - route, model, region
  - rollout_id
  - config diff summary (redacted for secrets)
  - gate_run_id + Console link
  - reason code and top 3 failure reasons

Observability / audit
- Emit events:
  - rollout.promotion_blocked (reason_code, gate_state)
  - rollout.auto_rollback_triggered (reason_code)
  - rollout.auto_rollback_failed (error)
- Ensure events include stable identifiers: route_id, account_id (if applicable), model_family, model_version, diff_hash.
- These events should be referenced by audit log pipeline (ENG-3927).

Acceptance criteria
- Promotion is blocked when gate is FAILED / NOT_FOUND / PENDING / RUNNING.
- Promotion succeeds only when gate PASSED or OVERRIDDEN (with non-expired override).
- If gate fails after canary begins and auto_rollback_on_gate_fail is enabled, rollback to previous stable is initiated within 2 minutes.
- All blocks/rollbacks emit an audit event with reason codes and can be correlated to gate_run_id.
- Console can show a user-readable failure reason derived from reason codes + gate summary.

Testing plan
- Unit tests: gate decision logic (states, mismatch, TTL, override expiry).
- Integration tests (staging):
  - Start rollout with canary at 1%, gate pending -> promotion attempt blocked.
  - Gate passes -> promotion unblocks.
  - Gate fails with canary live and auto rollback enabled -> rollback executed.
  - Override granted, then expires -> further promotions blocked.
- Chaos-ish test: Optimize service briefly unavailable at promotion time -> rollout remains halted (no promotion), retries backoff.

Implementation notes
- Coordinate with Jordan Lee / Benji Okafor on policy evaluation surface (per-route tier defaults).
- Coordinate with Chloe Martin / Felix Schneider on deep link format for Console (gate_run_id + rollout_id).
- Security review: confirm no sensitive prompt/eval artifacts are leaked to unauthorized viewers; links should be authorized through Console (not direct object store URLs).

Links
- Confluence PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/optimize-quality-guardrails-gating-prd.json
- System design: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/optimize-quality-gates-system-design.json
- Related tickets: ENG-3921, ENG-3927, ENG-3925
- Implementation PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-19544-rollout-controller-respect-quality-gate-for-promotion.json

Rollout plan
- Stage in internal beta: enforce on 2 internal routes (one batching change, one quant profile change).
- Limited production rollout: enforce for hosted API subset (self-serve) with auto rollback on gate fail.
- Expand to enterprise once override/audit + support tooling is stable.
comments: 2025-12-09 (Paula Mendes): We need defense-in-depth here. Optimize UI blocking is not enough; rollout controller must refuse to promote without a PASSED/OVERRIDDEN gate. Please prioritize reason codes so Support can explain blocks without digging through logs.

2025-12-17 (Sean Gallagher): For MVP, do NOT page on “promotion blocked” unless it affects >N active rollouts or lasts >2h. Page only on rollback failure. Add a metric for blocked promotions by reason_code to feed alerts.

2026-01-08 (Hannah Rivera): Implemented gate lookup at promotion time with 30s cache + exponential backoff when Optimize service is unavailable. Unknown/NOT_FOUND defaults to block. Added HALTED_QUALITY_GATE and reason codes.

2026-01-21 (Jonas Weber): Please ensure mismatch detection includes baseline_ref and model_version, not just diff hash. We’ve seen accidental reuse of a gate run across different baselines in early testing.

2026-02-06 (Marcus Lin): Security note: artifact links must be Console-authz’d. Rollout controller should store artifact IDs or Console deep links, not raw object storage URLs. Approved approach in PR-19544.

2026-02-18 (Hannah Rivera): Marking Done. Merged PR-19544. Staging verification complete: (1) pending gate blocks promotion, (2) failed gate triggers halt, (3) auto rollback works for self-serve policy, (4) override expiry blocks subsequent promotions. Follow-up: ensure dashboards pick up new reason_code tags (tracked in ENG-3926).
